races.name: Sky Bet "Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe" Handicap Stakes (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good heart after a win 19 days ago, wears a visor, and has a solid record in similar going (12/15 runners placed); Mark Walford's yard is firing at 3/14 over 14 days and the horse's best form has come at six furlongs, so dropping to five at York on fast ground is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Lethal Nymph
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, Paul Midgley-trained and returning after 34 days; the STYLE_FIT flag notes it is racing somewhat out of role here, and its recent form reads 604852, but the clear lead and absence of pressing rivals is its biggest asset — the question is whether it has enough raw ability at this level.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's consistent hold-up five-furlong specialist is returning 19 days after a run, and Charlie Todd takes the ride; wins have come on standard and good ground (1/5f/GOO in the last five), and its record at the trip is strong enough to make it interesting from the back if traffic cooperates.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: A prominent type with an excellent record at five furlongs on good ground — three wins and six places from 11 similar-going runs — trained by Paul Midgley who has recent winners, and Jonathan England rides; 15 days since last run looks sharp rather than rushed given the form string reads 303123, including a recent win.

runners_data.name: Roberto Caro
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose best form has come on softer surfaces (SOF/STA dominates the history), and the fast York ground today is a concern; Sean Flanagan rides for Adrian Keatley and the OR=78 mark looks achievable in theory, but the going tag includes a tongue-tie and the five-furlong trip is shorter than his recent outings.

runners_data.name: King's Call
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with an alarming recent record of 0/0/0/0/0 across similar going — 13 of 15 similar-going runs have yielded no wins or places; the hold-up style compounds the worry in this shape and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will need a flawless run from what looks a difficult position.

runners_data.name: Mon Na Slieve
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this Kevin Ryan five-furlong hold-up type who has solid course-form (7/5f/GOO, 3/5f/GOO recently) and a 1W2P record in similar going; came third and fifth in its last two York runs at this distance and could be competitive if given a smooth passage through the field.

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for Antony Brittain who finished second over five furlongs at Southwell recently and has placed once in eight similar-going starts; Sean Quinlan rides and the horse's natural front-running inclination should allow it to sit comfortably behind Lethal Nymph — the concern is whether it has a genuine turn of foot on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type carries a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, ran nine times over five furlongs on good ground for 2W3P, but recent form shows a 9th and 7th from the last two outings; Dylan Johnston takes the ride on a horse whose going record looks fine but whose current form may not be at its peak.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: Danny McMenamin rides this horse whose true style is genuine hold-up, though it appears in midfield on the map due to the crowded rear — its actual five-furlong form on good ground is very strong (6/7 placed, 1W3P), including a recent win, and on ability alone it warrants respect if it can find the daylight its style demands.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old is by nature a closer, pushed into a mapped midfield position because of the density of rear-of-field types in this field; the form book shows consistent five-furlong placing on good ground (2W in last five, multiple seconds at the trip) and Kevin Brogan rides — the style displacement is the main risk, not the ability.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls trains this four-year-old whose natural hold-up style is displaced toward the midfield on the map given the volume of closers entered; Brendan Powell rides and the record over five furlongs on good ground is excellent — 2W3P from 12 similar runs — making it one of the most interesting horses if it travels into the race.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's nine-year-old veteran is a true hold-up horse appearing further forward on the map than it would naturally settle; OR=71 is workable and the 9/15 similar-going record shows consistency, but age and a 34-day absence for Tristan Durrell's partner suggests this is one needing everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's lightly raced four-year-old carries headgear (p) and boasts a recent win — 1/5f/GOO in the last five starts — with a profile that reads as a genuine closer; James Best rides and while the horse's natural style is hold-up, it has placed heavily on good ground (1W4P from 7/14), suggesting enough class to cope if traffic breaks its way.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Harry Reed partners this seven-year-old trained by Tristan Davidson, back 14 days after a run; the five-furlong good-ground record is modest (1W2P from 4/15), and while its natural deep position means it needs a strong pace to mow down rivals, there is no such strong pace on offer here today — a difficult profile for this shape.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old ran only five days ago, which is the shortest turnaround in the field, and carries a tongue-bar and blinkers; the good-ground five-furlong record is the best of the redistributed hold-up horses (3W6P from 12/15 similar runs), but Richie McLernon must navigate 17 runners having been mapped out of its preferred deep position.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: Tom Tate's ten-year-old is a veteran prominent racer — 1W7P from 12 similar-going starts — and Caoilin Quinn rides; the horse's best form has come at six furlongs on good ground, and dropping to five at York is a potential concern, though its front-running inclination means it could sit handily behind Lethal Nymph and get involved in the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Lethal Nymph is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field over York's straight five furlongs on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rival willing to press hard from the gates, Jonathan Burke can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop that plays directly to hold-up horses getting a predictable rhythm to aim at. Kodiac Thriller, Emerald Harmony, Sports Coach and Bayraat will press forward into prominent positions behind Lethal Nymph, creating a bunched group just off the pace rather than a messy scrap for the lead. The redistributed hold-up types — Managing Director, Cayman Tai, Tees Aggregates, Ventura Express, Cameley Days, Harb and Dream Deal — are genuine closers by nature but will be unable to settle as deep as they prefer in this large field, forcing them into a midfield berth that is neither their natural style nor ideal; of these, Managing Director and Cayman Tai have the best recent form to capitalise if they get a clear run. With a single front-runner setting a measured pace on fast ground at York, this shape decisively favours prominent racers who can track just off the leader and kick from a position of cover, rather than true hold-up horses trying to make up ground through a wall of 17.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lethal Nymph Controls, Prominent Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Lethal Nymph is undisturbed in front and the pace is steady enough that horses tracking just behind can sustain momentum into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lethal Nymph sets a clean, metronomic gallop and the horses sitting second or third — Emerald Harmony and Kodiac Thriller — get a perfect tow before unleashing their finishing effort inside the final furlong on the fast ground; York's straight five rewards horses that travel into the race rather than have to find extra from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drops, Hold-Ups Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lethal Nymph goes too steady and the field concertinas, allowing the genuine closers to close the gap through a gap-ridden finish.
scenarios.body: A truly slack gallop invites the redistributed hold-up horses to travel closer than expected, turning the race into a sprint for home where superior finishing speed over five furlongs on good-to-firm counts; Cayman Tai and Tees Aggregates, both with strong five-furlong form on this going, carry the best profile of the closers to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference in the closing stages and winners emerge from horses who find the clearest passage rather than the ideal tactical position.
scenarios.body: Seventeen runners over a straight five furlongs creates genuine crowding risks, and horses with recent course experience and agile jockeys who spot daylight early will pick up best when gaps briefly open; Mon Na Slieve and Almaty Star, both with solid five-furlong form on similar going, suit this scenario as hold-up types who can thread through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace suits Lethal Nymph so well that the tracking horses never fully close and the leader simply gallops them into the ground.
scenarios.body: York's straight five is kinder to front-runners on fast ground than most tracks, and if the prominent horses behind fail to coordinate their challenge, Lethal Nymph's race fitness off a 34-day break and Paul Midgley's good recent form could see it simply not come back to the field; this is the least likely shape given the strength of prominent rivals but cannot be dismissed entirely.

watchPoints.text: Lethal Nymph sets the entire pace narrative — if Jonathan Burke is headed or pushed into a faster-than-intended gallop by Kodiac Thriller or Sports Coach in the first furlong, the race shape changes entirely and the prominent runners will find it much harder to sustain into the final furlong.

Managing Director and Cayman Tai are both genuine hold-up horses displaced into the midfield by the crowded rear of the field — if either secures an unobstructed run down the centre of the track at York in the final two furlongs, their strong five-furlong form makes them live dangers that the market may underrate.

Tees Aggregates has an excellent record at the trip on this going (2W3P from 12 runs) and Brendan Powell is a capable jockey — watch how much racing room it gets in a 17-runner straight-five cavalry charge, as it could easily be the best horse beaten if caught in traffic.

King's Call carries a bleak record across the board and is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a prominent jockey booking does not change the underlying data and punters should be cautious about any drifting price masking genuine ability concerns.

Dream Deal ran just five days ago — the shortest gap in the field — and Tim Easterby regularly runs horses back quickly in sprints, so the turnaround alone is not a red flag, but watch the market to see whether connections are confident it has bounced back fully from what was a midfield finish last

races.name: Sky Bet Dash (Class 2 Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Pocklington
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over course-and-distance at Southwell recently; Joanna Mason retains the ride and the horse simply needs to replicate that front-running performance on Good to Firm at York, where the going suits, though its OR has crept up to 100 and finishing form of 78 raises questions about resisting challengers.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: James Doyle in the saddle is an upgrade; Hugo Palmer's 14-day strike rate of 3/32 is moderate but this 4yo has placed in six of its last ten on good ground and slots into the prominent group with tactical flexibility, though the 7f run last time suggests trainer may be testing stamina boundaries.

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's consistent 4yo has finished second twice and third once in its last five on Good ground over this exact trip; Rossa Ryan takes over and the horse's reliable prominent style means it should find a clean berth just off the pace without scrambling — the 9/10 sim-going record is compelling.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who relies on a late rattle and Daniel Tudhope knows the type well; the 8yo's best recent effort was a 3rd at Pontefract, and at OR 94 it needs to find more than it has shown lately, but a compressed field where the prominent ranks collide hands it a scenario to exploit.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who ran just 8 days ago at Haydock; the application of a p-hood and Connor Beasley's aggressive style means it will try to hunt a prominent pitch, and the two-placed efforts this season show it is in decent nick despite age, though the quick turnaround and trip back to 6f from 5f is a factor.

runners_data.name: Coul Angel
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 4yo is a model of consistency at the 6f trip on Good ground with a 1W3P record in sim-going; Clifford Lee has ridden it to places before, and the horse's style means it will attempt to go forward from the off and should not be squeezed out in the prominent battle.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: Steps up from 5f to 6f where its two course wins came over this trip; visor applied and P J McDonald is a strong booking, but the Geoff Oldroyd trainer 14-day rate of 0/1 is thin and the recent form of 5-1-0-5-3 over 5f leaves a question about whether the extra furlong suits now.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Ran only five days ago when third at Catterick, so freshness is not a concern; the David O'Meara 4yo won over 6f on Good ground earlier this season and Kieran Shoemark should be able to find a prominent berth, making it one of the better-placed runners if pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 6f on Good and Soft ground recently; Paul Mulrennan knows the horse well and the 3/8 placed-and-win record in sim-going is outstanding — a genuine prominent runner whose recent trajectory makes it a leading player if it can hold its early position in a crowded field.

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: In-form 5yo who won last time over this trip on Good ground; however, the field's surplus of prominent types means it is unlikely to secure its natural position early — Warren Fentiman (3) claims 3lb, and if it cannot recreate its front-running role the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 is a meaningful caution.

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo has placed five times in its last six starts including two wins; David Allan is reliable in these handicaps and the horse's progressive OR-93 represents genuine class for its age — sits naturally in the prominent group and won over this exact course configuration in June.

runners_data.name: We Never Stop
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides this genuine hold-up type for Kevin Ryan; recent form is patchy including two unplaced efforts at Goodwood, but the 2nd over 6f Good earlier this season shows the trip and conditions are fine — its fortunes depend entirely on whether closers can find a clear run through 22 runners.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who won over 5f soft and placed at 6f; the headgear (tp) helps it concentrate, but the overcrowded prominent ranks mean it is unlikely to get anywhere near its preferred position — Rowan Scott will need to be patient in a role this horse has rarely been asked to fill, hence the 0.93 style-fit flag.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: James Sullivan rides a 6yo who genuinely wants to bowl along from the front; Ruth Carr's record over 14 days is solid at 3/17, but the horse that wants to race prominently is being pushed into a midfield slot by circumstance — only two placed efforts in 15 Good-ground runs reflects a horse that struggles when denied its role.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8yo ridden by 7lb claimer Toby Moore; the visor headgear is applied and the horse has placed over 6f Good ground twice in its last five, but the 0W2P sim-going record and advancing age suggest it needs everything to go perfectly — genuine closer in a race where closers face a tough draw.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo has a strong strike rate of 3W5P in sim-going and ran just 15 days ago; Lauren Young (5) claims 5lb, and despite this horse genuinely wanting to be up with the pace, the congested prominent group means it will be shuffled back — the apprentice rider's ability to adapt mid-race is key here.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4yo is a consistent placer over 6f Good ground with 1W4P; ran only seven days ago in solid form and the visor headgear helps; Mark Winn rides and this horse's true hold-up style means it will settle at the back and look for a split — the 10/15 sim-going record is an asset.

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Stephen Hanlon's Irish 3yo won over 8f at the Curragh and placed over longer trips; this is a notable step down in trip to 6f and the horse is a genuine front-runner by nature being fitted with a hood, but the redistribution to midfield reflects that it cannot realistically lead in this field — the distance contraction from 8f is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby veteran who placed twice over this trip at Southwell last season; Duran Fentiman rides and the 8yo wears a p-hood to help focus, but it has failed to win in 15 Good-ground starts and is another natural prominent type shuffled back by circumstance, with a 0/0 sim-going W record offering little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Utmost Respect
runners_data.note: 288 days off the track is a significant flag for this 3yo; Amie Waugh (3) claims 3lb and the horse did win over 5f Good at Redcar on its return once before, but returning from near a year off in a 22-runner competitive Heritage Handicap is a stern test of Fahey's training sharpness.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie rides a 6yo who has placed twice over 6f Good ground recently and won over the trip; the horse is a natural front-runner being pushed back by field size, and while the redistribution note tempers its chance in this shape, its experience and course-familiarity could still see it sneak into a pocket if the crowd bunches ahead.

runners_data.name: Rock Opera
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall (5) claims 5lb for Fahey's yard; the 6yo has a creditable 1W6P record over 6f Good ground and won over this exact course in July 2023 — another horse squeezed from its preferred prominent position by field depth, but its track record here is better than its current OR-76 suggests and it could be underestimated.

races.paceDynamic: Pocklington is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 22-runner field, will be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being seriously pressured early — a controlled, honest tempo on Good to Firm ground at York is the most likely outcome rather than a true searching pace. That setup will compress the race into a flat-out dash from the two-furlong pole, suiting horses who can sit just off the tempo and sprint through with a clear run rather than those forced wide or buried in traffic. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than can physically claim those rails positions — Musical Touch, Evening Blues, Trilby, Rousing Encore, Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone, Havana Rum and Rock Opera all want to race prominently but will be shuffled back or wide; of those, Red Spells Danger, Novello Lad and Commanche Falls have both the class and draw credentials to actually secure early prominent berths. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-handy horses who can sit second or third off Pocklington's moderate lead, maintain a straight course down the stands side, and punch off the bridle in the final furlong hold the decisive structural advantage; closers face a traffic lottery in a compressed 22-runner sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pocklington Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Pocklington sets a measured front-running tempo that keeps the field bunched, allowing well-placed prominent runners to sprint past inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Pocklington's uncontested lead creates a false-pace gallop that suits horses in second to fourth early who travel with cover and attack the final furlong on the bridle; the Good to Firm surface rewards those with a quick, clean action rather than grinders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Pocklington converts its uncontested lead into a genuine wire-to-wire performance, setting just enough pace to string the field without capitulating late.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground at York the strong galloping track suits a horse who has dictated and relaxed, and Pocklington's recent win from the front at Southwell shows it can lead and score; the lack of any pressing rival means it never had to race in a manner that drained its reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed field creates significant late interference, allowing the genuine hold-up horses to find daylight in the final furlong when the pack spreads.
scenarios.body: Apollo One, We Never Stop and Yes I'm Mali are true hold-up horses who will sit off the entire field and rely on a gap appearing over the final furlong on the wide outside; on Good to Firm York this is viable if pace holds and the front rank ties itself up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent types jostle for position early, creating checks and stumbles that shuffle the field and allow a mid-price improver to steal the race in the carnage.
scenarios.body: The overcrowded prominent ranks create bumping and checked runs through the first two furlongs, gifting a clear passage to a horse wide or drawn kindly who accelerates at a moment when rivals are still recovering; Rock Opera and Havana Rum, both experienced on the track, could capitalise if traffic bunches across the stands rail.

watchPoints.text: Novello Lad — back-to-back 6f wins on Good/Soft and Paul Mulrennan retained; if it secures a prominent berth in the early rush it becomes the principal danger to all.
Red Spells Danger — progressive Tim E

races.name: Sky Bet York Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Royal Champion
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran returning after 90 days off, his record at 1m on good shows consistent front-running wins and he has the profile to control this from the front at his own pace; Clifford Lee's booking is key and the uncontested lead suits him perfectly, though rivals will be watching him closely for the kick.|

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old arrives in good form off a 39-day break with two wins at 9f on good ground and strong going figures of 7/9; James Doyle can place him handily just off Royal Champion's shoulder, and this track, trip and conditions all look straightforwardly suitable for his style.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: The sole genuine hold-up horse in the race, Dancing Gemini needs pace to aim at but his recent form — 5th, 4th, 6th, 13th — makes it hard to be enthusiastic; headgear is noted (p) and Roger Teal's 14-day strike rate of 0/9 adds no confidence, with his best chance being the one scenario where the front rank ties itself up.|

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old has a strong going record of 7/7 on good ground and won over 1m4f last time in that sphere, but his last two runs at Group level have been badly below form; in reality a prominent-style horse, he has been pushed into a midfield-mapped position here because Royal Champion and Damysus will be ahead of him, meaning he is unlikely to produce his best.|

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's lightly-raced three-year-old arrives on the back of three consecutive wins including over 1m on good ground, and at just 128lbs carries the lightest weight in the field; a naturally prominent-going type who won't easily get that position against older, higher-rated rivals today — his chance depends on Rob Hornby finding a position close enough to the pace to deploy his evident turn of foot.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Champion is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners over 1m2½f at York on good-to-firm ground, Clifford Lee can dictate an entirely uncontested, measured gallop from the front — there is no natural rival to push him along and the tempo will be controlled rather than searching. Damysus and Item are both genuine prominent types who will likely slot in just behind Royal Champion in the early stages, creating a compact, orderly procession rather than a contested pace scenario. The field holds more front-running and prominent-style horses than can all secure their natural position — Item and Pride Of Arras are both true prominent racers pushed into the midfield map because Royal Champion and Damysus will absorb those berths, meaning their ability to produce their best form is compromised by race shape. A controlled, single-file gallop on fast ground at York over this trip strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and possess a sharp, clean turn of foot when the tempo quickens in the straight — the true prominent profile and any horse with tactical versatility at this trip is ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Champion sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the race develops into a straight-line speed test from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Royal Champion dictates every yard at a sustainable pace and the horses travelling just behind him — Damysus in particular — are perfectly poised to pounce when the tempo lifts inside the final quarter-mile on good-to-firm ground; this shape rewards horses with a clean, economic racing style and a reliable turn of foot rather than those who need genuine pace to organise their effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dawdle Then Dash
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole, favouring the sharpest accelerator.
scenarios.body: Royal Champion crawls in front, the field concertinas behind him, and the outcome is decided by raw speed over the final two furlongs rather than class or stamina; Damysus, with his strong form at 8-9f and good-to-firm record, has the profile to quicken in this scenario but Item's youth and upward trajectory also make him dangerous if he can get a clear run from a midfield-adjacent position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Champion goes too fast for the conditions — unusually given his profile — or misjudges fractions and the race becomes a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: If genuine pace is set and maintained, Dancing Gemini's hold-up style becomes relevant as horses in front tire in the closing stages; Dancing Gemini has struggled recently and his OR has slipped, but he is the only true closer in the race and this is the one scenario where his natural style aligns with the shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Item or Pride Of Arras aggressively push forward and force a genuine pace duel with Royal Champion, scrambling race positions.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested pace would string the field out and could leave Royal Champion and other early movers weakened, theoretically opening a window for a fresh-legged closer — but with Dancing Gemini in poor recent form and Pride Of Arras running out of character, this scenario is low-probability and relies on multiple horses behaving against their mapped roles; Pride Of Arras has the stamina for 1m2½f and a good-to-firm record but has badly underperformed recently.

watchPoints.text: Royal Champion's pace control is everything — if Clifford Lee rolls along unchallenged at a crawl, he becomes very hard to pass and the race could be won and lost in the opening half-mile of tempo-setting.

Item and Pride Of Arras are both natural prominent racers who cannot all get their position — watch the first two furlongs to see whether either pushes forward, as any pace flare-up would significantly alter the race shape.

Damysus's last run was a fifth in a Listed race at 8f which looked below his best — if that run was a blip he is the main threat to Royal Champion, but if it signalled a loss of form his chance deflates sharply.

Dancing Gemini's headgear (p — presumably a hood or similar) is worth monitoring in the paddock; if it settles him better than recent runs suggest, he is the only horse in the race who structurally benefits from a hot pace scenario.

Going is officially Good To Firm throughout the card — fast-ground conditions at York over 1m2½f historically favour horses with a clean, economical action and a reliable turn of foot, which profiles Damysus and Royal Champion most closely.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 4yo for John Butler who has landed two places from four runs on Good ground over this trip; Connor Beasley is a shrewd booking, 16 days since last run, and if he gets a clean prominent pitch behind Paladin this is a realistic threat.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby hold-up type with a solid recent record over 7f on Good but stepping up to 1m today; 15 days since last run, David Allan takes over, and the mile trip on fast ground is a genuine question mark against a horse who has raced shorter.

runners_data.name: Paladin
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner from Kevin & Lauren Frost, last won at Sandown over 8f on Tapeta and the STYLE_FIT flag signals he can race out of role — but here that role is exactly what he is asked to fill; Rossa Ryan can dictate his own terms and two wins in five recent runs give him clear claims if he gets it soft in front.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 4yo hold-up mare who won over 8f on Good and has placed four times in 15 similar-going runs; Christian Howarth (3lb claim) reduces the weight, she has been off 31 days, and she will need the pace to lift to deliver her challenge from rear.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby 5yo who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though placed here in midfield due to the overcrowded rear; STYLE_FIT flag applies as the race shape is unlikely to produce the late surge he requires, having won over 10f on Good just recently and dropping back in trip on only 6 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Prominent 6yo wearing a visor for Gihan Arnolda who has been remarkably consistent at placing (1W3P from 8 similar-going runs) over 7-8f on Good; 14 days since last run and if he can prise a handy pitch he has the profile to stay competitive throughout.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 5yo wears a hood and has won twice at this sort of trip on Good ground; Paul Mulrennan takes the ride, 20 days since last run, and from a prominent position he could keep finding for pressure if the pace is sensible.

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne

races.paceDynamic: Paladin is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival capable of seriously contesting that position from the off, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around York's flat mile. Final Night and Cancan In The Rain will push to race prominently behind him, with Dwindling Funds and Rajapour also keen to sit close to the pace, meaning the prominent berths are competitive but the overall tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. The field is unusually hold-up-heavy — Financer, Barry's Boy, Draupnir, Up The Jazz, Barley and Kiss Me Love are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there is no room for all of them at the rear; Paladin and Final Night are the likeliest to actually secure their natural positions. A controlled pace set by Paladin on Good to Firm ground at York — a track that consistently rewards horses ridden close to the pace — firmly favours prominent racers who can travel into the race comfortably and quicken from the front two furlongs out; genuine hold-up horses will find the pace insufficient to generate the late sectionals they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Paladin Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Paladin dictates an uncontested lead and the pace is modest enough to reward those travelling just behind him.
scenarios.body: Paladin sets a measured clip on the Good to Firm surface and the race is effectively run to suit those who have been racing in his slipstream from the outset; York's flat mile puts a premium on those positioned within two lengths of the leader at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Paladin is pressed hard enough that the pace lifts and midfield travellers get a true-run race.
scenarios.body: Cancan In The Rain or Dwindling Funds push the tempo in the back straight, turning the race into a genuine test where those with cover in midfield find themselves in the right position at the right time; horses such as Rajapour and Canvas, who track the pace effectively, become the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick and legs tire in the final furlong, opening a late run from deep.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop burns through the prominent horses and the leaders come back to the field in the closing stages, giving hold-up types a rare opportunity to close on this track; Kiss Me My Love and Up The Jazz, who have the best recent form in similar conditions over this course and distance profile, would benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Split Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 17 splits into groups and positional luck dictates the outcome.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners on the straight York mile, some horses will find themselves shuffled wide or squeezed at a critical juncture, and an unexpected winner could emerge from a runner who simply finds a clear run at the right moment; Bowood and Montezin, both held up in recent runs and with modest claims on form, could sneak a place in a messy affair.

watchPoints.text: Paladin's early position is everything — watch whether Rossa Ryan takes him straight to the front unchallenged or whether Cancan In The Rain or Final Night push him into a faster clip than intended, which would transform the race shape entirely.

Rajapour has run just 6 days ago and races again here; watch for any signs in the paddock or early gallop that the quick turnaround has left a mark, as his chance depends on travelling smoothly from a prominent pitch.

The 17-runner field creates significant traffic risk rounding the final bend — watch how riders positioned mid-to-rear, particularly Up The Jazz and Kiss Me My Love, navigate gaps in the straight, as a blocked run would cost either of them dearly.

Financer, Barry's Boy, Draupnir, Up The Jazz, Barley and Kiss Me My Love are all genuine hold-up horses unable to get their preferred positions — watch whether any of them drift wider than expected in the back straight as jockeys attempt to secure cleaner air.

Good to Firm conditions confirmed for this race — watch whether any trainer withdraws a hold-up horse who genuinely needs cut in the ground, as several in this field have mixed going profiles and the fast surface could be an inconvenience for a handful of them.

races.paceDynamic: Tycoon is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine rival willing to dispute the lead, he should be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, self-determined tempo on Good to Firm ground at York. Behind him, four runners — Likealot, The Glen Rovers, Ashnak, and Caliban — all want to race prominently, creating a congested group between the leader and midfield that raises the risk of traffic interference and shuffling two to three furlongs out. Damascus Steel I and Therapist are genuine prominent types who cannot all find their natural berth and have been mapped to midfield, meaning the race shape they would ideally exploit is less freely available to them. With Tycoon likely to set an honest but unhurried pace over this staying trip on a flat track, the race shape strongly favours horses with the tactical versatility to travel prominently in behind and quicken under pressure from two out — patient prominent types with a turn of foot hold the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tycoon Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tycoon leads unchallenged and sets a measured tempo that suits prominent chasers who can peel off his back.
scenarios.body: Tycoon dictates at a sustainable clip and the prominent group — Likealot, Ashnak, Caliban — travel comfortably within striking range before mounting their challenge inside the final two furlongs; the flat York straight rewards those who have conserved energy racing close to the pace. Caliban, who has won twice over similar staying trips on Standard, and Likealot, progressive over 12f, are ideally placed structurally to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Tycoon goes overly fast early and ties up in the straight, leaving a vacuum for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Wahdan and Humble Spark, both genuine hold-up types, would find themselves with a wall of beaten horses ahead of them at the two-furlong pole and would need a clear run materialising late; on a flat course where genuine pace typically compresses late gaps, this is a secondary but credible outcome if the fractions are truly fast. Humble Spark's consistent placing record in similar conditions and Wahdan's York course form make them the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses all push for position early and create a scrappy, uneven pace that suits a horse who settles just off the bunching.
scenarios.body: The congestion in the prominent group causes interference two to three furlongs out, creating gaps and momentum shifts that a nimble, well-ridden horse can exploit; Ashnak, who has placed twice in Good ground over similar trips, could thread through as jockey Daniel Tudhope navigates the traffic. The Glen Rovers, reuniting with James Doyle and proven over 10f at York, could also find daylight if the chaos plays into his hands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Find Room
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I or Therapist manage to secure a prominent berth despite the field's structural congestion.
scenarios.body: Both horses are natural prominent racers whose in-form profiles — Damascus Steel I has won twice in his last six — could translate into competitive showings if the prominent group is smaller in practice than the map suggests; however, their redistribution penalty and Therapist's 175-day layoff mean this scenario carries meaningful execution risk. This shape requires fortune in running and the field thinning ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion (Likealot, The Glen Rovers, Ashnak, Caliban) — four runners competing for roughly two or three ideal spots mean significant interference is possible at the 2-3f marker; any horse squeezed or checked at that point could lose all momentum on the flat York straight.

Tycoon's lead uncontested — if Toby Moore (7lb claimer) misjudges the tempo and allows too slow a pace early, the race could turn into a sprint home from 2f out, entirely changing which profiles benefit.

Caliban's 137-day absence — despite two recent wins on Standard, he has not raced on Good to Firm and has been off the track since autumn; watch the market move and his pre-race condition carefully as a fitness doubt could undermine his structural positional advantage.

Damascus Steel I and Therapist — both horses will likely be racing away from their ideal prominent position; watch if either drifts wide to find daylight early or makes an unexpected move before the turn, as that tactical adjustment will be the key to whether their form translates.

Therapist's market — a 175-day layoff combined with a redistributed prominent style means any significant market support would warrant attention, as connections may have targeted this specific Good to Firm York opportunity with a planned return to form.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Noble is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press him hard from the off over York's 7f, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable clip that keeps the tempo honest without turning this into a true test of stamina. Flight Control, Return Of The Gods and Invincible Boy are all confirmed prominent types who will want to race close to the pace, and their presence means the first two furlongs will be occupied but not frantically contested. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Toastmaster, Raging Raj, Dacres Cross and Forest Phoenix are genuine prominent horses who are most likely to concede ground at the start and settle in a chasing pack rather than secure their natural position. The result is a race likely to be run at a steady-to-fair gallop with a compressed mid-race, which on Good to Firm ground at York strongly favours horses who can race prominently, travel with cover just off the pace, and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — the prominent to mid-division profile with a clean passage is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Noble controls a fair gallop and the prominent closers like Flight Control and Return Of The Gods track him without burning fuel, the race sets up for a clean, strong-finishing prominent type.
scenarios.body: Mr Noble's uncontested lead rolls into the straight at a pace that suits horses who have relaxed just behind — Flight Control's consistent York form and Return Of The Gods' recent winning burst at 7f both fit this shape perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers

scenarios.body: A compressed pack turning in would set up a strong late surge for horses like Gunalt Wavelength or Bleep Test who have the finishing kick to close ground rapidly on fast ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mr Noble Makes All
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Noble is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a truly controlled, measured gallop, his front-running style could prove impossible to peg back on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: York's 7f favours front-runners who can quicken into the straight without having been pressured, and Mr Noble's recent winning form and Burke's strong 14-day record give this real weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crowded Mid-Race Collision
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types push forward and create an early scrimmage, the pace becomes ragged and the race breaks apart unpredictably.
scenarios.body: A messy, fast early pace would catch the prominent pack out and could hand a surprise opportunity to a hold-up horse drawn wide with clear daylight — Thankfully or Milford Grange could sneak into contention.

watchPoints.text: Mr Noble has never raced beyond 6f — watch his behaviour in the final furlong at 7f, as if he ties up it reshapes the entire race and Flight Control or Return Of The Gods would be immediate beneficiaries.

Toastmaster and Raging Raj are both natural prominent types who are likely to be shuffled back — if either or both push forward and create an early pace surge, the gallop could become significantly stronger than expected and benefit the hold-up horses.

Milford Grange is a hold-up type with all meaningful form on Soft ground; if the Good to Firm description is accurate following the going report, this horse may simply not handle the surface and could be a false market runner.

Gunalt Wavelength's 3lb claim for Joanna Mason is worth monitoring in the market — at these low weights any reduction is meaningful and the horse has two wins at this exact trip/going combination in its last five runs.
